source.title: PatchBench: Measuring Collateral Damage in Activation Patching
source.authors: Alexi Canesse; Mathis Le Bail; Maël Jenny; Clément Elliker; M. El Sharkawy; S. Vanier

page_placements.theme: Safety steering by adding refusal or safety vectors at inference: gains, over-refusal and capability costs, gating

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present
record.tranche_reason: The study applies activation-steering interventions and measures their effects on refusal of harmful prompts, refusal of nearby benign prompts, and MMLU performance. It does not perform the original all-layer, all-position ablation.
record.gate_note: The study measures added steering methods, including an AlphaSteer difference-in-means refusal direction, but does not directly test the original harmful-minus-harmless direction with ablation and addition. Background descriptions of prior work are not results from this study. No weight-edit/abliteration or jailbreak-suppression experiment is reported.
record.test_reason: This is a benchmark paper on how precisely safety patches repair jailbreak failures. It applies four existing refusal-steering methods as tools and scores them on its own HNCS/BNPS metrics and MMLU. None of the vectors is the original harmful-minus-harmless difference-in-means direction. AST and CAST add a PCA direction from refusal- vs compliance-suffix contrasts on benign prompts. AlphaSteer and AdaSteer use refused-minus-complied harmful prompts, and AlphaSteer passes it through a learned, prompt-dependent null-space map. There is no directional ablation, and no test of whether one direction mediates refusal. Steering strengths and layers are tuned per model to trade correction against benign preservation. The results therefore describe patch performance, not whether V1 holds. The reader's 'tests/T2' and V1 labels should be dropped.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that activation patching can strongly improve correction of nearby harmful variants while causing benign-neighbour over-refusal, even when MMLU barely changes. Patches should be evaluated as local repairs, with correction and preservation measured separately.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates several steering constructions rather than the original all-layer, all-position projection ablation. AlphaSteer uses a difference-in-means refusal vector based on harmful prompts the model refuses versus complies with, plus a benign null-space projection; AST uses refusal/compliance suffix contrasts; AdaSteer and CAST add adaptive or conditional mechanisms. Steering is applied only at selected layers. The paper describes the methods as activation steering/patching, not weight edits.
record.method_sensitivity: Results differ by model and steering method. In a supplementary generator comparison, HNCS and BNPS values vary between Mistral Large- and GPT-4o-generated neighbourhoods; the authors report marginal differences and stable aggregate rankings. The paper also reports Llama-4-Scout scaling results, omitted from the extracted rows due to the row limit.

fits_no_version.finding: Adding refusal vectors (suffix-contrast PCA or refused-minus-complied diff-in-means) at middle layers raises refusal on harmful jailbreak variants. HNCS rises from 18-40% unsteered to 58.5-95.6% across four instruct models (Table 1).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Adding related refusal vectors induces refusal on near-variants of jailbreak prompts in 3-8B instruct models.

fits_no_version.finding: The same additions also cause refusal of nearby benign prompts. BNPS drops from 97-99% to as low as 28.4% (unconditional AST, Gemma 4B). Some of this over-refusal is lexical and some structural (Figure 6).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Refusal-vector steering used as a safety patch over-refuses benign prompts that share wording or structure with the harmful prompt.

fits_no_version.finding: MMLU cost of tuned steering ranges from -0.07 to -21.62 points. Unconditional AST costs 6-22 points; gated CAST costs at most 3.4 (Table 2).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The capability cost of refusal-vector addition depends on whether and how it is gated.

record.code_released: not stated (the paper says code is available on GitHub but gives no URL in the text)
record.problems: The main results are fixed benchmark measurements with no error bars. They use 50 source failures per evaluated model and a WildGuard-based refusal scorer; the paper reports a human validation of that scorer. MMLU is a coarse capability check, and the paper notes sensitivity to hyperparameter choices.
record.rows_left_out: To stay within 60 rows, omitted Table 5 generator-comparison HNCS/BNPS rows, Table 6 aggregate generator comparison, Table 7 Llama-4-Scout HNCS/BNPS rows, Table 2 unsteered MMLU rows, and Figure 6 benign lexical-versus-structural breakdown. The omitted generator comparison and Llama-4-Scout results are in Appendices C.2 and D; MMLU baselines are stated in Table 2 and retained in the intervention rows' baseline fields.

untested.parts: Harmful-minus-harmless direction, ablation removing refusal, and single-direction mediation are not tested. Addition is done only with other refusal vectors, at tuned middle layers.

record.verdict_notes: The paper cites Arditi et al. only as background. Its AST implementation follows Lee et al. (CAST), with the vector built from refusal and compliance suffixes on benign Alpaca prompts. The 'refusal direction' in AlphaSteer and AdaSteer contrasts harmful prompts the model refuses with harmful prompts it complies with, not harmful with harmless. Steering strengths and layers are tuned on validation to balance refusal and benign acceptance, so the magnitudes reflect tuning choices. The Llama-4-Scout results (Table 7) and the generator comparison (Tables 5-6) are declared in rows_left_out. Tranche T4 is applied loosely: the methods are not the authors' own, but the study uses them as tools and reports their patch performance.

versions.untested_parts: Tests steering additions and their local refusal and MMLU effects, but not the original harmful-minus-harmless direction, ablation at every layer and position, or ability beyond MMLU. It does not isolate whether one direction alone mediates refusal.
No test of attacks suppressing the direction or training against its ablation.
AdaSteer uses an additional harmfulness-related direction, but the study does not test whether refusal is better described by an affine structure, cone, or multiple refusal directions.
No experiment testing whether harmfulness judgment is encoded separately from refusal.
No cross-language or base-to-instruct transfer test of the direction.
No comparison of training procedures or training stages for whether a removable direction exists.

relation.reason: It cites Arditi et al. as the basis for AST and uses refusal steering as the intervention under evaluation. Its results concern whether patches are locally selective, not whether a single diff-in-means direction mediates refusal.

tranche.reason: Benchmark paper. It applies four existing refusal-steering methods as tools and scores them on its own HNCS/BNPS and MMLU. AST/CAST use a pairwise-PCA refusal-vs-compliance-suffix vector from benign Alpaca prompts. AlphaSteer/AdaSteer use a refused-minus-complied harmful diff-in-means. None is the harmful-minus-harmless direction, and no version's question is posed.

source_check.notes: The record header gives code: n, but the text says code is released on GitHub (the URL was lost in extraction). On Llama-4-Scout (App. D) the trade-off flips: AlphaSteer has the lowest BNPS (74.8) and AST keeps 94.5, so the AST over-refusal pattern is not uniform across models. The authors_conclusion paraphrase matches Sec. 6.

statements.correction: Unsteered HNCS 18.2-40.1; steered HNCS 58.5 (CAST Gemma) to 95.6 (AST Qwen); unsteered BNPS 97.1-99.2; min BNPS 28.4 (AST Gemma 4B); AST MMLU drops 6.20-21.62 pp; CAST drops 0.07-3.44 pp. Llama-4-Scout (App. D, Table 7): CAST HNCS 44.6, AST BNPS 94.5, lowest BNPS AlphaSteer 74.8; no MMLU reported for Scout.
statements.problem: All numbers match Tables 1-2 for the four main models (Qwen 3B, Mistral 7B, Llama 8B, Gemma 4B). The statement does not say its ranges leave out the Llama-4-Scout appendix, where the pattern differs.
